findings.description: STK-SUP-012 requires a fault code, affected entity and timestamp for every detected fault. OP-SYS-014 still supplies no approved frame, code and entity mappings, or timestamp definition. OP-SYS-016 supplies no reporting deadline. CON-SUP-007 defines the serial line settings only.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-014 and OP-SYS-016. Define how to verify one complete report for each detected fault, including faults involving multiple tasks and reports completed after a reset.

findings.description: The status response required by STK-SUP-013 depends on OP-SYS-017 for the request and response encodings, status fields, sampling instant and deadline. Those criteria remain open, so the stated test cannot determine whether the response represents current supervision status.
findings.requested_change: Approve the status interface and timing in OP-SYS-017. Include the expected outcome when a request is received shortly before a reset.

findings.description: OP-SYS-018 leaves the retained count, encoding and response deadline open for the history requested by STK-SUP-013. The statement also counts reports at request reception but leaves membership unspecified when a report is recorded during response preparation.
findings.requested_change: Approve the history contract and define the snapshot instant used for both the count and the identity of the returned reports. Verify requests with empty, partial and full histories and a report recorded while a request is being handled.

findings.description: OP-SYS-012 leaves the program-code regions and corruption-detection criteria open. The injection test therefore has no basis for deciding whether the start-up check covers the program-code corruption required by STK-SUP-007.
findings.requested_change: Approve the covered code regions and detectable corruption classes. Specify the observed detection event, including in a corrupted start-up that never starts an application task.

findings.description: OP-SYS-012 leaves the configuration-data regions and corruption-detection criteria open. The injection test therefore has no basis for deciding whether the start-up check covers the configuration corruption required by STK-SUP-007.
findings.requested_change: Approve the covered configuration data and detectable corruption classes. Specify the observed detection event, including in a corrupted start-up that never starts an application task.

findings.description: STK-SUP-008 requires repeated, bounded full passes. OP-SYS-019 gives no approved bound, and OP-SYS-020 gives no coverage against which to establish that a pass is full. The test checks reported completion times alone and could accept repeated partial passes.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the pass bound and coverage. Specify evidence that every covered area was checked in each timed pass.

findings.description: STK-SUP-008 requires preserving application timing. OP-SYS-021 leaves the quantities, baseline, limits and accepted target timing evidence open. The proposed simulator comparison cannot establish an interference verdict from the current inputs.
findings.requested_change: Approve the protected timing quantities, workload, baseline, limits and evidence accepted for target timing. Align the paired-run test with that decision.

findings.description: The recovery clock uses output switch-off and status-signal change events. During a failed start-up, SYS-SAF-003 can already hold the status signal at not-operational, so there may be no change event to start the recovery clock required by STK-SUP-010.
findings.requested_change: Define the safe-state entry instant when either indication is already in its required state. Use that event consistently for the recovery clock and verify a failed start-up with the indications already safe.

findings.description: OP-SYS-022 supplies no approved recovery bound or decision for a watchdog reset that starts before safe-state entry is complete. The STK-SUP-010 verification also cites only SYS-TST-002, which no longer injects memory faults.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the recovery bound and the disposition of a watchdog reset before safe-state entry. Cover start-up and run-time memory faults using SYS-TST-004 and SYS-TST-005, as well as the task faults.

findings.description: The latch required by STK-SUP-010 depends on an unresolved threshold, fault-equivalence rule and run-clearing rule in OP-SYS-023, and an unresolved release condition in OP-SYS-024. There is no test oracle for which entry latches the controller or which event may release it.
findings.requested_change: Approve the latch threshold, fault-equivalence rule, counted entries, run-clearing events and release condition. Include the treatment of a failed start-up when the outputs and status signal already indicate the safe state.

findings.description: OP-SYS-025 leaves the workload, window and accepted target cycle evidence open for the STK-SUP-014 limit. The analysis also assumes selected simulator runs reach the longest paths. Observed runs alone cannot establish worst-case target cycle counts.
findings.requested_change: Approve the reference workload, window and target cycle evidence. Require a justified upper bound for execution counts and cycle costs, including interrupts and peripheral waits, across the specified windows.

findings.description: STK-SUP-011 requires distinguishing three reset causes, but OP-SYS-026 and OP-SYS-027 still leave cause discrimination, precedence and the observation contract open. The stated tests use isolated causes and cannot verify the precedence rule for simultaneous indications.
findings.requested_change: Confirm the available cause evidence, precedence and observation contract. Verify supervisor-requested reset discrimination and each supported combination that invokes precedence.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-001 detects an alive fault when the first completion is missing, but the SYS-SAF-001 timer starts only from a preceding completion. That completion does not exist in this case, so the 50 ms output-off obligation from STK-SUP-009 has no applicable start event.
findings.requested_change: Use both alive-fault expiry events from SYS-SUP-001, including expiry from the alive-supervision start instant, and verify output switch-off for a missing first completion.

findings.description: The STK-SUP-009 output-off test relies on unresolved output criteria and fault instants in OP-SYS-028 and OP-SYS-029. It cites SYS-TST-002 for run-time corruption even though that item now injects task faults only. The stated initially-on precondition is also unqualified for failed start-up.
findings.requested_change: Approve the output-off criteria and fault instants. Reference the memory stimuli in SYS-TST-004 and SYS-TST-005 and define the verdict for outputs already off at the fault instant.

findings.description: The status-signal timer for SYS-SUP-001 assumes a preceding completed execution. SYS-SUP-001 also detects a missing first completion. For that case the 50 ms status deadline required by STK-SUP-009 has no applicable start event.
findings.requested_change: Use both alive-fault expiry events from SYS-SUP-001 and verify the not-operational indication for a missing first completion.

findings.description: OP-SYS-029 and OP-SYS-030 leave the accepted timing origin and physical indication unresolved for STK-SUP-009. The test cites SYS-TST-002 for run-time corruption and cannot exercise that stimulus after the injection requirements were split.
findings.requested_change: Approve the status indication and fault instants. Use SYS-TST-004 and SYS-TST-005 for the memory cases and verify the 50 ms outcome against the same fault instants as SYS-SAF-001.

findings.description: The hold derived from STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-009 depends on the unresolved physical indication, reset release and pre-software evidence in OP-SYS-030 and OP-SYS-031. The test also cites SYS-TST-002 for start-up corruption, which only SYS-TST-004 now specifies.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the indication, reset boundaries and accepted evidence before software configures the pin. Use SYS-TST-004 for both failed start-up checks and cover each applicable reset class.

findings.description: OP-SYS-032 leaves the first-completion timing for STK-SUP-001 provisional. The stopped-scheduler test also expects an alive fault for every task in one run, although recovery after the earliest fault can reset the controller before other configured intervals expire.
findings.requested_change: Approve the first-completion timing and observe the alive detection for each target task before any reset that would prevent its deadline from expiring.

findings.description: A start at or after the scheduled time can satisfy the stated guard even if the start belongs to a later activation of the same task. When the configured delay spans another scheduled activation, the missed instance can escape late-activation detection under STK-SUP-002. OP-SYS-033 leaves this unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Define which start satisfies each scheduled activation, or approve and enforce a limit that prevents overlap. Test a missed activation followed by the next instance starting.

findings.description: The main overrun cases accept the safe outputs and status as evidence. An alive or program-flow fault can produce the same reaction while execution-time detection is absent. The tests therefore do not establish detection of the execution-time violation required by STK-SUP-002.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the timing definition in OP-SYS-034 and verify a specifically attributed execution-time detection before completion, including a case that also crosses another supervision threshold.

findings.description: The order-check trigger uses any expected instance of a control cycle. It identifies neither the first eligible cycle after start-up nor whether the check applies while latched. SYS-SUP-005 explicitly restricts skip checks to supervised cycles, and OP-SYS-035 leaves the order-check scope open under STK-SUP-003.
findings.requested_change: Approve the operating states and first eligible cycle for order checking. State whether SYS-SUP-004 uses the same supervised-cycle predicate as SYS-SUP-005 and test the first eligible cycle.

findings.description: The STK-SUP-003 skip tests accept the common safe-state reaction, which an earlier late-activation or out-of-order fault can cause even if skip detection fails. OP-SYS-035 and OP-SYS-036 also leave the cycle and cutoff rules pending approval.
findings.requested_change: Approve the cycle and cutoff rules and verify a skip-specific detection or approved combined classification at cycle close. Include an instance starting exactly at the boundary.

findings.description: The demonstration for STK-SUP-015 accepts the listed task stimulus and the common safe-state reaction. An injection can cause several violations, so that observation cannot show that each intended SYS-SUP-001 to SYS-SUP-005 condition was actually produced and detected.
findings.requested_change: For each injection, verify the intended trigger from the schedule and execution trace and attribute the observed detection to that trigger, including cases with overlapping faults.

findings.description: OP-SYS-038 leaves the approved timeout range and first-interval behavior unresolved. The positive tests also accept a controller reset within the range without requiring attribution to the independent watchdog. A supervisor or window-watchdog reset can satisfy that observation while the STK-SUP-005 fallback fails.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the first-interval behavior and timeout criteria. Attribute each positive test reset to the independent watchdog and compare it with the timeout configured for that run.

findings.description: OP-SYS-039 leaves the initial window reference, opening range and reset latency unresolved. The positive test for STK-SUP-006 observes a controller reset without requiring the window watchdog to cause it.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the opening, start and latency criteria. Verify that an attempt just below the configured opening causes a window-watchdog reset and that an attempt at the opening is outside the early-fault condition.

findings.description: OP-SYS-039 and OP-SYS-040 leave the window start, closing settings and reset latency unresolved. The positive test accepts any reset no later than the calculated deadline, even one before the closing instant or caused by another reset source. This does not establish the late-service reaction under STK-SUP-005 and STK-SUP-006.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the window and latency criteria. Require an attributed window-watchdog reset between the configured closing instant and the approved latency limit, for both the first and a subsequent window.

findings.description: The independent-watchdog service test depends on the unapproved timeout lower limit in OP-SYS-038 and the health and start-up criteria in OP-SYS-041. In particular, the first healthy instant may follow the earliest permitted timeout, before SYS-WDG-008 permits servicing. STK-SUP-005 cannot be verified with the current timing inputs.
findings.requested_change: Approve the health evidence and timeout limits. Verify that first permissible servicing can occur strictly within the independent-watchdog bound for the longest supported healthy start-up.

findings.description: The STK-SUP-005 inhibit begins at the detection instant and covers rejected window-watchdog attempts. OP-SYS-042 leaves detection instrumentation open, and SYS-TST-006 records servicing rather than every attempt. With that trace, a late inhibit or a rejected attempt during the inhibit can escape the verdict.
findings.requested_change: Define accepted observations of each fault detection and every watchdog service attempt. Verify the inhibit across the detection boundary and until the next reset, including a fault that later clears.

findings.description: SYS-RST-001 exposes a single watchdog-reset class. OP-SYS-015 leaves open what evidence identifies the triggering watchdog event, what entity and timestamp the report carries, and whether event subtypes must be distinguished. OP-SYS-016 also leaves the deadline open. STK-SUP-012 cannot be verified from the reset class alone.
findings.requested_change: Approve the report mapping, pre-reset event evidence and post-restart deadline. Verify the expected report for each of the three watchdog stimuli against the independently observed event.

findings.description: After an interrupted report the item requires transmission after restart, but neither the statement nor OP-SYS-016 defines the outcome if the next reset interrupts the retry. This matters for the repeated resets contemplated by SYS-WDG-008 and the per-fault reporting obligation in STK-SUP-012.
findings.requested_change: Define report identity and delivery across successive interruptions, the reset classes covered, and how the SYS-DIAG-001 deadline applies. Confirm the retention needed for that behavior.

findings.description: Recording is allowed before transmission completes, and SYS-DIAG-006 can retransmit the same report after a reset. With OP-SYS-018 unresolved, recording before interruption and again after retransmission can produce either one or two history entries for the same detected fault under STK-SUP-013.
findings.requested_change: Define the event that commits a history entry and whether retries share the original entry. Verify the history after an interrupted transmission and a completed retry.

findings.description: The history retention derived from STK-SUP-013 depends on an unresolved retained count and reset retention capability in OP-SYS-018 and OP-SYS-016. OP-SYS-026 also leaves the classification of several reset causes open. The item has no demonstrated retention criterion covering all resets in its scope.
findings.requested_change: Approve the retained depth and retention boundary by reset class. Confirm supporting platform evidence and verify that record identity and recency survive each covered reset.

findings.description: OP-SYS-020 gives no approved run-time coverage or detectable corruption classes for STK-SUP-008. The test cites detection by pass completion but identifies neither a detection observation tied to the injected corruption nor how to judge a pass that terminates on detection.
findings.requested_change: Approve the run-time coverage and corruption criteria. Define the observable detection and the pass endpoint on both clean and failed checks, then verify detection against that endpoint.

findings.description: STK-SUP-010 requires safe-state continuity until power cycling. The item applies to each non-releasing reset, but its test covers only simulator-supported causes. OP-SYS-024 still leaves the retention and board evidence for output and status continuity during reset and before software runs unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the power-cycle boundary and accepted evidence for both indications through every non-releasing reset. Include the other-reset class of SYS-RST-002 and provide evidence for applicable cases outside simulator coverage.

findings.description: The STK-SUP-010 latch release depends on an unapproved power-cycle condition in OP-SYS-024. The test accepts eventual application start after passing checks, which does not establish that the latch ended at the stated restart event or that protection remains effective when start-up checks fail after release.
findings.requested_change: Approve the power-cycle signature and restart event. Verify latch release at that event separately from application start authorization, including a release followed by a failed integrity check.

findings.description: The other-reset class protects the distinctions required by STK-SUP-011, but OP-SYS-026 does not establish the applicable causes or the evidence that distinguishes them. The test restricts its coverage to modeled causes and can succeed without assessing a supported cause omitted by the simulator.
findings.requested_change: Approve the cause-to-class mapping and required evidence. Verify each applicable other-reset cause through SYS-RST-003 or specify accepted evidence for causes the simulator cannot reproduce.

findings.description: A request fully received an instant before the next reset qualifies for a complete response, even when the reset interrupts the serial transmission. OP-SYS-027 leaves that request outcome undefined. The test for the STK-SUP-011 observation interface sends requests without a further reset.
findings.requested_change: Define the request eligibility and outcome when a reset interrupts the response, together with the approved observation and timing contract. Verify a request received immediately before a reset.

findings.description: The 50 ms output-off timer from STK-SUP-009 uses the last independent-watchdog servicing, which does not exist on the first timeout after reset under SYS-WDG-002. It also uses early window-watchdog servicing, which can exclude a rejected early attempt that triggers SYS-WDG-003.
findings.requested_change: Use the SYS-WDG-002 interval reference instant for timeouts and the SYS-WDG-003 attempt instant for early events. Verify both a first-interval timeout and a rejected early attempt using the approved output-off indication.

findings.description: The status deadline from STK-SUP-009 inherits the SYS-SAF-004 event definitions. They provide no origin for a first independent-watchdog timeout without prior servicing and can exclude an early window-watchdog attempt rejected under SYS-WDG-003.
findings.requested_change: Use corrected event definitions shared with SYS-SAF-004. Verify the approved not-operational indication within 50 ms for both start-up timeout and rejected early-attempt cases.

findings.description: The reset-time hold derived from STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-009 applies from the instant reset starts. OP-SYS-030 and OP-SYS-031 leave the indication, supply threshold and permitted transition time unresolved. A reset-state pin value alone cannot establish the required indication throughout the transition.
findings.requested_change: Approve the indication, reset boundaries and any transition allowance. Verify the transition and the full reset interval using the platform pin behavior and board circuitry for each reset cause.

findings.description: The early-event stimulus is described as a servicing, which SYS-WDG-003 defines as an accepted attempt. A rejected early attempt can trigger the hardware reset and is within the STK-SUP-015 injection scope, but the stated stimulus and servicing trace can miss it.
findings.requested_change: Define the early stimulus as the pre-opening service attempt regardless of acceptance. Demonstrate that the corresponding simulated watchdog caused the first reset, with evidence for the attempt and its timing.

findings.description: The simulator obligation covers any tester-selected corruption within the approved start-up classes, but neither the domain in OP-SYS-012 nor the pre-release injection capability in OP-SYS-037 is established. Demonstrating a selected subset alone does not establish selectable coverage for the start-up faults in STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-015.
findings.requested_change: Approve the eligible regions and corruptions and confirm injection before reset release. Verify representative injections in both memory categories and substantiate the claimed selection range.

findings.description: The STK-SUP-015 demonstration places a corruption after its area was checked in the current pass. SYS-TST-006 records pass starts and completions only, so the trace cannot establish the required relative placement. OP-SYS-037 item (f) still leaves per-area observability open.
findings.requested_change: Define accepted evidence for when the targeted area was checked and correlate it with the injection timestamp. Verify both injection timings and substantiate the supported corruption selection.

findings.description: The requirement promises every listed event, but its demonstration checks only that each event kind that occurred is present. A trace can omit an individual task completion, reset or diagnostic byte and still meet the stated demonstration for STK-SUP-015.
findings.requested_change: Verify event counts, identities and order against an independent event sequence and check timestamp accuracy against the accepted simulator time resolution.

findings.description: The service band needed by STK-SUP-005 and STK-SUP-006 depends on unapproved opening and closing limits in OP-SYS-039 and OP-SYS-040 and the health transition in OP-SYS-041. The test has no approved band or evidence that a legal first attempt is possible when health is first established.
findings.requested_change: Approve the service band and health transition. Verify feasibility of the first permitted service in the start-up window and test attempts at both edges of the approved band.

findings.description: The inhibit ends when every configured task meets the SYS-WDG-005 predicate. Neither STK-SUP-004 nor SYS-SUP-006 states a minimum task count. If an empty task set is permitted, the universal predicate can hold without any completed execution or supervised cycle, bypassing the intended STK-SUP-005 start-up inhibit.
findings.requested_change: Define the permitted task-set cardinality and the health and inhibit behavior for an empty or invalid task set. Verify that start-up servicing follows the approved rule.
